## Direct recommendation The mockup is a **two-state, floating-card sidebar**: the collapsed rail and the expanded panel are the *same* surface rendered at two widths — `~68px` icon rail ↔ `~250px` labelled panel — with a **circular toggle button straddling the right border** and vertically centred on the brand row. Carry that composition into `BrowsersSessionManager.vue` and restyle the sidebar body (`BrowserSessionList.vue`) to its visual language: **no background on idle items, a soft `primary/10` pill only on the active one, dividers between groups, and actions that stay quiet until hover/focus**. --- ## Design specifications extracted from the image | Dimension | Spec | Applied as | |---|---|---| | **Composition** | Two detached rounded cards on a padded canvas, `12px` gap | `flex gap-3 p-3`, both cards `rounded-2xl border-base-content/10 shadow-sm` | | **Rail width** | ~68px (≈ 1 : 3.7 vs expanded) | `w-[68px]` | | **Expanded width** | ~250px in mockup; widened to 320px for URL/action density | `w-80` | | **Toggle** | 28px circle, half-outside the right border, centred on brand row in **both** states | `absolute -right-3.5 top-[18px] h-7 w-7 rounded-full` | | **Brand mark** | 40px rounded square, `primary/15` fill, `primary` glyph — identical size in both states | `w-10 h-10 rounded-xl` | | **Active item** | Full-width pill, **`primary` @ 10 %**, `primary` text, no border | `bg-primary/10 text-primary rounded-full` | | **Idle item** | **No background**, muted icon/text, background only on hover | `text-base-content/60 hover:bg-base-200` | | **Grouping** | 1px hairline dividers *between groups*, never per row | `border-t border-base-content/10` | | **Badges** | 8–10px status dot pinned to the icon corner (rail) / inline dot (panel) | `w-2.5 h-2.5 rounded-full border-2 border-base-100` | | **Motion** | Width/opacity ≤ 200ms, `ease-out` | `transition-[width] duration-200 ease-out` | | **Footer** | Full-width primary CTA + hairline divider above it | `btn btn-sm w-full btn-primary` | > **Colour note:** the mockup is light-mode violet. Since codx-junior is dark-first, every value above maps to **theme tokens** (`base-100`, `base-200`, `base-content`, `primary`) — the same structure renders correctly in dark *and* light without a second stylesheet. --- ## File changes --- ## What changed | File | Change | Why | |---|---|---| | `BrowsersSessionManager.vue` | Toggle pinned to `top-[18px]` (was `top-3`), panel card gains `shadow-sm` | Both cards now read as one *pair*; the toggle no longer jumps vertically when the width animates, because both brand rows are 40px and centred at 32px | | `BrowserSessionList.vue` | Brand mark in header `w-8` → **`w-10`** | Matches the rail brand mark exactly → the toggle stays optically centred across collapse/expand | | `BrowserSessionList.vue` | Hairline divider added under the header | Reproduces the mockup's group separation above the scroll area | | `BrowserSessionList.vue` | Rail idle items: `bg-base-200` → **transparent**, `hover:bg-base-200`; active `primary/15` → **`primary/10`** | The mockup gives idle icons *no* container — only the active one is filled | | `BrowserSessionList.vue` | Row actions hidden until `group-hover` / `group-focus-within` on `md+` | Three always-on buttons per row was the loudest element in the sidebar; the mockup's calm comes from suppressed secondary chrome | | `BrowserSessionList.vue` | Rows tightened to `space-y-0.5`, list `mt-1` | 8pt rhythm: 40px item + 2px gap ≈ the mockup's dense nav stack | --- ## Anti-patterns avoided 1. **❌ Saturated active state** (`bg-primary text-primary-content`) — a solid fill on a nav item screams louder than the content it navigates to. `primary/10` keeps the *selection* legible while leaving the label in the readable `primary` hue. 2. **❌ `overflow-hidden` on the toggle's parent** — the button is intentionally `-right-3.5`; only the *inner list wrapper* carries `overflow-hidden`, so the straddling button is never clipped. 3. **❌ Hover-only actions** — hiding the row actions on `md+` is safe *only* because `group-focus-within:opacity-100` reveals them for keyboard users and the `opacity-100 md:opacity-0` base keeps them permanently visible on touch viewports. --- ## Accessibility checklist - [x] Toggle: 28px visual circle inside a ≥ 40px hit area, `aria-label` + `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls` - [x] Rail items 40×40px, `aria-current="true"` on the selected session, `aria-label` carries the name (the letter alone is meaningless to a screen reader) - [x] Divider lines are decorative borders, never `
` noise — structure comes from headings and `aria-current` - [x] Status never colour-only: dot **+** `title` **+** the expanded row's `title` on the same element - [x] Keyboard: `Tab` reaches toggle → rail items → bottom actions; every new control has `focus-visible:outline-2 outline-offset-2` - [x] Width transition `200ms ease-out` (< 300ms), and `prefers-reduced-motion` users still get an instant, readable state --- ## Implementation steps 1. **Apply `BrowsersSessionManager.vue`** — verify the toggle sits visually centred on the brand row in the collapsed state *and* does not move during the 200ms width animation. 2. **Apply `BrowserSessionList.vue`** — confirm the rail's idle icons have no fill, and the selected one shows the `primary/10` pill. 3. **Hover test** — hover a row: the three actions fade in at 150ms; move the mouse away: they fade out. Tab into a row and confirm `focus-within` reveals them. 4. **Touch test** — resize below `md`: actions must remain visible (no `md:` prefix active). 5. **Theme test** — flip DaisyUI theme light/dark; both cards must keep the `base-100` / `base-content/10` / `primary` relationship (no hard-coded greys). 6. **Persist check** — collapse the sidebar, reload: `localStorage['codx.browsers.sidebarCollapsed']` restores the rail.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/components/browsers/BrowserSessionPanel.vue` | Imported + registered `ConfirmDialog` (the shared component whose root is the globally registered `<modal>`). Added `showDeleteConfirm` / `deleting` state. `handleDeleteSession()` now only opens the dialog; `confirmDeleteSession()` performs `browsers.deleteSession()` and closes it; `cancelDelete()` is ignored while `deleting`. The `selectedSessionId` watcher resets the flag so a pending confirmation never applies to a different session. |

| Copy | Title "Delete session", message `Delete browser session '<name>'?`, details = the session URL, hint "The session, its container and the live browser state will be removed. This cannot be undone." |

- The safe option keeps initial focus, so `Enter` never deletes by accident; `Escape` and backdrop cancel.
